title: Client Partnership Pulse + CEO Summary Template
body:
Purpose:
This one-pager + short email template is meant for C-suite recipients at our customers to summarize the last quarter and align on the renewal runway. Use as the cover note ahead of the Quarterly Partnership Review meeting or as a standalone executive recap.

How to use:
- Personalize the first paragraph to reflect relationship level (e.g., mention product lead or SRE champion).
- Swap metrics to reflect the customer’s primary contract KPIs (latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on eval set).
- For high-risk relationships, include an explicit remediation timeline and POC owner.

1) One-page 'Partnership Pulse' (to attach to invite or send as PDF)
- Header: Partnership Pulse — {{customer_name}} — {{quarter}}
- Top-line summary (2–3 sentences):
  • Overall status: Green/Yellow/Red and one-sentence rationale (e.g., "Green — Production latency stable; adoption up 28% since last quarter").
  • Impact highlight: short bullet quantifying business impact (e.g., "Saved ~US$26K in inference spend vs. baseline through batching+cache").

- Momentum metrics (4 quick tiles):
  • Usage: Monthly tokens processed — 1.2B (↑ 28% QoQ)
  • Latency: p50/p95/p99 for gen endpoints — 85 / 210 / 430 ms
  • Reliability: Service uptime — 99.94% (SLA target 99.9%)
  • Cost: Avg cost per 1k tokens — $0.19 (net of committed discounts)

- Adoption & product outcomes (3 bullets):
  • Feature adoption: Rewrites endpoint adopted by product team; 9k daily calls.
  • Quality signal: Eval set pass rate 81% (target 85%) — regression on two prompt clusters flagged.
  • Ops friction: Onboarding of internal users reduced from 6 to 2 days after sample training doc rollout.

- Renewal runway snapshot (one row):
  • Contract end: {{contract_end_date}}
  • Health score: 78/100 — drivers: usage growth (+), latency improvements (+), open quality bugs (-)
  • Recommended action: Move to annual committed capacity + Pilot Optimize module

- Risks and mitigations (short table style in text):
  • Risk: Model-quality regressions on edge prompts — Mitigation: Weekly eval + canary rollback policy (owner: ML eng: Diego).
  • Risk: Increasing peak load causing p95 spikes — Mitigation: Autoscale policy bump + temporary burst capacity (owner: SRE: Samira).
  • Risk: Contract budget cycles misaligned — Mitigation: Align finance sponsor + 60-day renewal alert (owner: CS: Priya).

- Asks (concrete call-to-action):
  1) Approve proposal for Dedicated pool pilot (30k/month) by {{decision_date}}
  2) Grant 1-hour exec sync with CTO + Head of Product within next 3 weeks to review roadmap impacts
  3) Share updated projected token volume for next 12 months (finance worksheet)

2) 20–30 minute Executive Sync Agenda (use for invite):
  - 0–5m: Welcome + top-line pulse (CS lead)
  - 5–12m: Business impact & adoption highlights (customer sponsor + CS)
  - 12–20m: Risk, remediation plan, and renewal runway (CS + SRE + ML)
  - 20–25m: Decision points & asks (clear yes/no/needs-more-info)
  - 25–30m: Next steps & owners

3) Email template — short customer-facing quarterly recap (subject + preheader + body)
  Subject options (pick 1):
    - "Partnership pulse: {{customer_name}} — Q{{quarter}} review"
    - "Quick update: performance, impact, and next steps ({{customer_name}})"
  Preheader: "Top outcomes, health snapshot, and two asks for the upcoming renewal"

  Email body (concise):
  Hi {{exec_first_name}},

  Quick note to share a short partnership pulse for {{quarter}}. High level: production traffic is up ~28% QoQ, average p95 latency improved by ~35ms, and we estimate a run-rate cost reduction of ~$26K thanks to batching + prefix caching.

  Attachment: one-page Partnership Pulse (PDF) with the full metric snapshot and suggested renewal runway.

  Two quick asks:
  1) Can we schedule a 25–30 minute exec sync in the next 3 weeks to align on renewal options?
  2) Please confirm who on your finance team is the point of contact for capacity planning.

  We value the partnership and want to make sure the technical roadmap matches your product timelines — happy to tailor the agenda.

  Best regards,
  Priya Rao
  Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

4) CEO-style one-paragraph to include in a high-touch customer email (more personal):
  "Dear {{exec_first_name}},

  It’s been a privilege to support {{customer_name}}’s rollout of large language features this quarter. The team’s rapid adoption and clear product outcomes have been impressive — from measurable latency wins to meaningful cost savings. I wanted to personally thank you for the collaborative approach and share that we’re fully committed to ensuring predictable economics and ironclad reliability as you scale. I’ll have our CS lead follow up with a brief to align on the best path to long-term committed capacity."

5) Suggested slide titles for a short exec deck (5 slides):
  - Slide 1: Partnership Pulse — Q{{quarter}}
  - Slide 2: Top 3 outcomes & customer quotes
  - Slide 3: Metrics snapshot (usage, latency, cost, reliability)
  - Slide 4: Risks & mitigation timeline (owners)
  - Slide 5: Renewal options & recommended next steps

6) Health score rubric (quick guide for CS)
  - >90: Excellent (green) — adoption accelerating, no production regressions, >99.9% uptime
  - 70–89: Caution (yellow) — adoption positive but unresolved quality issues or budget misalignment
  - <70: Risk (red) — active escalations, significant regressions, or churn indicators

Notes / rough checklist before sending to execs:
- Attach a one-page PDF generated from this doc (clean up numbers, hide internal-only rows).
- Run the partnership pulse past the solutions lead and SRE owner for sign-off.
- Confirm the finance contact and insert the correct contract end date & decision deadlines.
- Remove internal-only mitigation comments before sending to the customer.

Draft history / context (internal):
- Created to provide an alternative to longer QBR decks — aimed at time-pressed executive sponsors.
- Built from recurring requests: shorter email, clear asks, and a quantifiable renewal recommendation.

Quick checklist: (tick before send)
- [ ] Numbers validated with infra billing + product analytics
- [ ] Open incidents reviewed and summary added
- [ ] Exec sync invite created with agenda and owners

Open questions (for CS to resolve):
- Which exec should receive the CEO paragraph vs. the standard CS cover note?
- For customers with multiple product lines, do we send one consolidated pulse or multiple smaller pulses?

Owner notes: keep this doc succinct — the target audience is C-suite and procurement. Attach supporting slides only when asked.

---
